incident-bot: PAGE: Streaming tail latency alert for cluster=prod-streaming. p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 ~ 4.8s, SLO=500ms. Triggered 2026-03-15T09:12:57Z. Paging oncall: @jordan. Impact: intermittent SSE clients seeing delayed flushes and reordered chunks.

jordan (oncall): seeing it in dashboards. p99 spike aligns with increased connection churn on proxy nodes. :eyes:

alex (runtime): I can repro a replay of a connection that gets into a "drift" state where chunks queue up and don't flush until buffer full. Likely around proxy upstream keepalive timeouts + TCP RTOs.

maya (sre): customers reporting slow UI updates. Not full outage but high tail. Which routes?

samira (prod-eng): looks like streaming/chat and stream/generator routes—TaskFlow (enterprise) sent a spike that correlates. They saw heartbeats dropped and then a big flush.

jordan (oncall): quick check: `curl -s http://streaming-proxy.metrics/metrics | grep tail_latency` shows 95th=1.2, 99th=4.8. Also seeing connection resets: `proxymgr: upstream reset by peer` in logs.

alex (runtime): posting recent proxy snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T09:11:42Z proxymgr[62]: conn=0x7f3f keepalive_idle=16s upstream=10.2.3.7:5042 write_buf=8192 flush_pending=true
2026-03-15T09:11:45Z proxymgr[62]: conn=0x7f3f upstream reset by peer (code=RST)
2026-03-15T09:11:46Z streamhandl[201]: client=taskflow-123 SSE: pending_chunks=5 last_flush_age=3.4s
```

maya (sre): RSTs + pending_chunks explain flush delay — proxy holds until either buffer full or flush timer. If keepalive triggers RST then race happens.

samira (prod-eng): mitigation plan ideas: 1) increase proxy upstream keepalive/idle from 15s->60s for streaming nodes (reduce RST churn), 2) lower streaming proxy internal flush threshold (force flush every 50ms), 3) temporarily route TaskFlow traffic to a smaller pool with longer-lived conns, 4) disable batching for latency-sensitive streaming routes. Which is safest to try live?

jordan (oncall): I'm for quickest low-risk: adjust flush timer and disable batching per-route. We can patch via k8s rollout and monitor. If that doesn't hold, increase keepalive.

alex (runtime): I can push a runtime config change for flush timer via configmap. Command: `kubectl -n infra patch configmap streaming-proxy-cfg --patch '{"data":{"flush_ms":"50"}}'` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/streaming-proxy`.

maya (sre): I'll take the keepalive bump if needed. For now disable batching on TaskFlow routes: `rdctl routing update --route /v1/stream/taskflow --no-batching --force` (ops-bot will run).

ops-bot: Executing routing update: rdctl routing update --route /v1/stream/taskflow --no-batching --force
ops-bot: Routing update complete (id=deploy-4821). Rolling 2 replicas.

jordan (oncall): applied flush_ms=50 and disabled batching for TaskFlow. Watching metrics.

(2m) samira (prod-eng): slight p95 drop to ~650ms, p99 down to 2.1s. Still above SLO but trending good. TaskFlow reports fewer big flush events.

alex (runtime): also enabled proxy-level connection keepalive debug on one node to watch RSTs. If RSTs stop, that was the root cause.

maya (sre): FYI I see an increase in client backpressure signals from CDN side: `tcp_zero_window` spikes — clients choking. Could be client-side slow consumers exacerbating buffering.

samira (prod-eng): good note. We should add a mitigation: implement per-connection slow-consumer detection to drop/notify clients and avoid global tail blowup. Add to backlog if not immediate.

jordan (oncall): for immediate customer comms: Samira, can you send a short note to TaskFlow support with current mitigations and ETA? They asked for real-time updates.

samira (prod-eng): on it. Drafting: "We're seeing elevated tail latency on streaming endpoints caused by intermittent proxy connection resets and slow consumers. We've deployed per-route changes (disabled batching, lowered flush timer) and p99 improved from 4.8s -> 2.1s. Working on keepalive bump if needed. Next update in 20m."

jordan (oncall): keeping this incident page open. If metrics stabilize in 15m we'll close. Handing off in 20m to maya.

maya (sre): I'll take over at 09:33Z. If p99 stays <2s and no new RSTs, close after 30m.

alex (runtime): follow-up action items (quick): [1] add per-route no-batching opt toggles to runbooks, [2] add short-term guard to flush on every token for high-priority customers, [3] investigate client-side zero-window causes with CDN team.

ops-bot: kube rollout status deploy/streaming-proxy: 2/2 updated.

jordan (oncall): final note: put a prod alert to watch `streaming.conn.rst_rate` and `streaming.pending_chunks` with lower thresholds. Setting now.

samira (prod-eng): thanks team. Updating TaskFlow and ops runbook. Will include suggested long-term: persistent keepalives, slow-consumer eviction, and probe-based load shaping.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. p95 now 480ms, p99 1.4s. Next update in 20m or on escalation."
